agent: Theatre wave, collecting session: the military AI's first piece (2026-10-17)
question: What the AI's theatre layer draws - an area's fronts, a country's fronts, the theatres made from them and merged, matched and refreshed - and the theatre headquarters it adopts or makes; for OpenHOI3's stage 5, checked against the start save's area_theatre blocks.

addresses.name: COwnerArea::BuildFronts
addresses.comment: **An area's fronts, made afresh** - called for every area RebuildOwnerAreas makes (0x47D07D) and every area UpdateOwnerAreaOfProvince touches (0x47F36F, 0x47F95D, 0x47FD75). Frees +0x74 and +0x84, then over the area's provinces in order: one on a land border (CProvince_BordersForeignLand) and in no land front yet (COwnerArea_LandFrontOf) starts a new CAreaBorder on +0x74, filled by COwnerArea_FloodFront; one whose template has a sea province beside it (+0xA4) and in no sea front (COwnerArea_SeaFrontOf) starts one on +0x84 with `sea` (+0x18) set. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-theatres.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled and read: both list clears at the top, the two `new CAreaBorder` (0x2C bytes, vftable 0x15BDB60) arms, byte +0x18 = 1 only on the +0x84 arm, and the four callers by findRefs --callers. Ghidra's auto-name (CAreaBorder::CAreaBorder_2) came from the inlined vftable store. Wrong if a front ever appears in +0x74 not made here.

addresses.name: COwnerArea_FloodFront
addresses.comment: Pushes the province onto the front's vector (+0x8) and recurses, in the province's edge order and **whatever the edge's kind**, into each neighbour of the same area (+0x2B4) that: for a land front, is on a land border and in no land front of the area; for a sea front (+0x18), has a sea province of its own (template +0xA4) sharing a region with this one's sea province, or both with none, and is in no sea front. Depth first, so a front's provinces are in that walk's order. `ret 8`. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-theatres.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled; the recursion at the two call sites, the area test on +0x2B4, and the two membership helpers (EAX = area, EDI = province). Wrong if a kind-3 edge were skipped - no `cmp ..., 3` in the body.

Used by COwnerArea::BuildFronts and FloodFront, and by CTheatre_PickHQProvince (x2 to a candidate). The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-theatres.md, sections B and K.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled whole, 0x4A5E30-0x4A5F80, two `ret 4`. The edge loop reads no kind. Wrong if a sea neighbour could pass: it tests template +0x22 (is_land).

addresses.name: CollectAreaFrontsForCountry
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CollectAreaFrontsForCountry(COwnerArea* area, CList<CAreaBorder*>* out, CCountryTag tag)
addresses.comment: **A country's fronts of an area, made new** - not a filter. Over the area's land fronts (+0x74) and their provinces in order: a province's enemy is the controller across its edges not of kind 3 (simulated, land, not its own controller), a front-worthy one (CAIStrategy::IsFrontWorthyEnemy) replacing one that is not; it is **hot** where that controller is at war with the country or either is REB, which ends its walk. It then joins every border of `out` that is hot with it or has its enemy and that it touches (CAreaBorder_Touches): none - a new border at the end; several - each from the last back appended to the first and deleted, the first hot if either was. Then each hot border is given the area it faces (+0x24: the real area other than this one most edges reach, first of equals in pointer order), and appended to the first other hot border facing the same area. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-theatres.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Read on the listing 0x47DA40-0x47E4C6 (the decompiler's `free(...); return;` arms are list removals inside loops). Checked as built in OpenHOI3 against the start save's area_theatre fronts.

addresses.name: CAIStrategy::IsFrontWorthyEnemy
addresses.comment: **Whether a country is an enemy the theatre layer draws a front against.** In order: itself false; a subject - the answer for its overlord; IsWarCandidate true; IsFriend(tag, true) false; this a subject whose overlord is allied to it false; preparing war on it true; a scenario false. **In no faction**: FIN (NOR and GER false, SOV true) and JAP (CHC CHI CGX CSX KOR MAN MEN SIK CXB CYN true); a country we are at war with in a real faction - false; its faction real and not democracy's (GetIdeologies +0x34) true; JAP or ITA and no subject true; else true where floor((sqrt((d*d/1000 + d*d/1000)/1000.0f) + 0.0005)*1000) >= 180000 with **d the alignment x difference (+0xE4) both times**. **In a faction**: its faction real and another true; then a compiled-in table by our tag (all false within one faction) - SOV against FIN ROM POL EST LAT LIT SWE HUN BUL TUR YUG SLO CZE AUS MAN JAP, GER against HOL BEL LUX POL DEN, FRA against ITA BEL LUX, BEL against LUX, ENG against ITA, JAP against CHC CHI CGX CSX KOR MAN MEN SIK CXB CYN - the cached slots of CCountryDataBase::AddCountry, whose order past slot 28 is not the .rdata array's - with France's BEL and LUX and Belgium's LUX true only while Germany owns land, is outside our faction and is not at war with it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-theatres.md, section D.
addresses.evidence: Read whole on the listing 0x8A9390-0x8A9A29: the two IsFriend/IsWarCandidate calls, the 0x8A9599 faction fork, the tag table's cmp chains against CCountryDataBase's cached tag slots, and the x-only alignment arithmetic at 0x8A9962-0x8A9A10 (CCountry +0xE4 read twice, +0xE8 never).

See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-theatres.md, section D.

addresses.name: CAIStrategy::BuildTheatres
addresses.comment: **A country's theatres, made from nothing.** Nothing for REB or a zero id; in a running game with theatres and the flag clear (or the country played), RefreshTheatreProvinces and back. Otherwise per area of CCountry +0xD30: a theatre for each front-worthy front whose enemy's adjoining areas (spill) reach 8000 or 250 of its own (home); the four seats (Paris and Warszawa for GER, San Fransisco and Washington D.C. for USA); one for an area nothing claimed; the rest of the area to the nearest theatre it touches, then to any it touches; the fronts left split by theatre and given to them in id order. Then the areas and ports of each, the merging (the smallest under 30 provinces into the nearest, larger ones where they share their enemies or their fronts meet), the match against the old theatres (an overlap of 500 keeps the old id), the old left over deleted with their headquarters queued for removal, MaintainTheatres(strategy, true), and theatres_dirty cleared. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-theatres.md, sections E to H.
addresses.evidence: Read on the listing, 0x8A9B10-0x8ABC83; the decompiler's per-area tail and the merge are garbled by list frees, and both were read on the listing. Checked as built in OpenHOI3 against the start save's 108 area_theatre blocks.

addresses.comment: 0x515CC0 onward; manipulates the countries vector at +0x16C/+0x170 at its head and then runs a 45-arm string-compare chain over the hardcoded tag names at .rdata 0x15C1DE4 ('GER' ... 'NZL', immediately followed by 'countrydatabase.cpp'). Each arm that matches caches the tag into an 8-byte slot at the front of the database. **The slot is not the string's place in the array past slot 28**: read arm by arm (the string each compares, the store its match makes), slots 0-28 are GER ENG SOV USA JAP FRA ITA PHI CHI CHC CGX CSX KOR MEN SIK CXB CYN BEL LUX HOL POL ROM HUN BUL TUR YUG SLO CZE AUS, and 29-44 are MAN NZL CAN SAF AST DEN FIN SWE NOR EST LAT LIT SCH SPA SPR ETH (MAN's string is compared twice; its second arm stores to slot 29). The constructor 0x4024D0 zeroes the 45 id halves. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-theatres.md, section D.
addresses.evidence: Every arm read on the listing 0x516100-0x5178A0 by a scratch script pairing each `mov edx, <tag string>` with the store its compare's branch leads to. Checked: with this map OpenHOI3's theatres are the start save's for all 78 countries; with the array's order the Soviet Union had four for nine.

struct_fields.name: theatres_dirty
struct_fields.comment: **The same byte as CCountry +0x580** (the strategy is embedded at +0x48C). Set by CAIStrategy::ClearCollectedLists with its flag, which CCountry's constructor and reset pass - so every country starts dirty and a new game's first hourly pass builds its theatres; by a controller change in a real area (the old and new controller and each neighbouring owner); by infrastructure crossing 100 or 200; by CCountry::OnDiplomacyChanged; after a ten-day Rebuild; and by the war targets' recheck dropping a neighbour. Cleared by BuildTheatres and RefreshTheatreProvinces. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-theatres.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: CCountry::CCountry at VA 0x4CA834 calls 0x8A3DE0 with 1 on +0x48C; ClearCollectedLists sets +0xF4 under that flag; BuildTheatres' `mov byte [edi+0xF4], 0` at VA 0x8ABC4E.

struct_fields.name: sea_fronts_first
struct_fields.comment: The area's sea fronts, made by COwnerArea::BuildFronts beside the land ones at +0x74: coastal provinces flooded by shared sea regions, each CAreaBorder with `sea` set. Read by nothing the theatre layer reaches. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-theatres.md, section B.
struct_fields.evidence: BuildFronts clears +0x84 and appends the `sea` arm's borders to it; COwnerArea_SeaFrontOf walks it.

struct_fields.name: sea
struct_fields.comment: Set on a sea front (COwnerArea +0x84). Saved as the front's `sea`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-theatres.md, section B.
struct_fields.evidence: BuildFronts writes byte +0x18 = 1 only on the +0x84 arm; FloodFront branches on it; every constructor zeroes it.

struct_fields.name: faced_area
struct_fields.comment: For a hot front of a country, the area it faces: the real area other than its own that most edges from its provinces reach. Hot fronts facing one area are merged. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-theatres.md, section C.
struct_fields.evidence: CollectAreaFrontsForCountry writes it at VA 0x47E369 and compares it at 0x47E3DF.

struct_fields.name: ports_first
struct_fields.comment: The theatre's provinces with a naval base, the largest first (CTheatre_InsertPortByLevel); last at +0x98, count at +0x9C. Made by CTheatre_RebuildAreas. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-theatres.md, section G.
struct_fields.evidence: CTheatre_RebuildAreas clears +0x94/+0x98/+0x9C and inserts there; CTheatre::TakeOver moves it.

struct_fields.name: orphaned
struct_fields.comment: Set by CGameState::RemoveUnit on each child of a removed level-0 unit (VA 0x68500E); a new level-0 headquarters made by CCreateNewHQCommand::Execute attaches every unit of the country so flagged under it and clears it. The constructor zeroes it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-theatres.md, section K.
struct_fields.evidence: A scan of every byte store to [reg + 0x50] in functions touching units: the constructor, RemoveUnit and the command are the only ones on CUnit.

struct_fields.name: unit_names_in_use
struct_fields.comment: The set of names the country's units, brigades, ships and wings are called, which RegisterUnitName adds to (0xB4A2E0) and CCountry::MakeUnitName asks (0xA86F70) - a name is taken only within its country. The container's own layout was not read. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-theatres.md, section K.
struct_fields.evidence: RegisterUnitName's `add edi, 0x84` on its country argument at VA 0x4CB4E0, and MakeUnitName's `add ecx, 0x84` on its country at VA 0x4CB6EB.
